RJR Interoffice Memorandum

SUBJECT: Overview and Recommendations of Next-Steps Team on Nicotine Review Meeting

DATE: February 23, 1989

TO: Dr. W. M. Hildebolt
Dr. A. W. Hayes
Dr. M. E. Stowe

FROM: T. A. Perfetti
W. M. Dufour
J. H. Reynolds
J. H. Robinson
J. S. Gentry
G. R. Green
D. L. Potter
C. A. Blixt

COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATIONS:

I. Establish a permanent interacting committee comprised of Strategic Marketing personnel from Tobacco USA and the Development Corporation and a selected group of product developers and research scientists that have a broad knowledge base and practical orientation. Their first objective would be to develop a co-ordinated 5 Year strategic plan on nicotine related projects. Their plan should encompass means to anticipate future consumer demands and means to link these emerging consumer demands to R&D technology development. Cooperation will be paramount.

II. Continue information exchange between basic researchers and product and applied researchers. Regular meetings, off-site, should be scheduled with specific divisions designated by product/research areas, e.g. LN, XGT, NN, etc., to present and exchange ideas/results which work toward the product/research goals.

III. Develop a continuing education program for scientists through cross training, not only in R&D, but with outside departments as well, to achieve a working knowledge of the technological base of information and its link to consumer demands. The current educational efforts such as the "Tobacco Training Course", the "Marketing Training Course", and the "Cigarette Design Course" are very important, yet they are like kindergarten courses in many ways as they merely present a very condensed version of known material, the simple building blocks of our industry. The continuing education program envisioned would not only provide the "brick and mortar", but also a blue print and engineers to build the highly innovative, high technology products needed by the industry.
